svg.title: A shopper buys running shoes in Gemini: UCP checkout, an AP2 checkout mandate (per spec), Google Pay, signed order webhooks
svg.desc: Sequence diagram: A shopper buys running shoes in Gemini: UCP checkout, an AP2 checkout mandate (per spec), Google Pay, signed order webhooks. 7 participants: Shopper, Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent), Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface), Google Pay (credential provider), Merchant (business, merchant of record), Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor), and Card network and issuer. 14 steps, 10 crossing a trust boundary, 9 failure branches. Based on several protocols UCP v2026-08-25 AP2 v0.2 (2026-08-25). Step 1: Shopper to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Ask for running shoes. Step 2: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): GET /.well-known/ucp (business profile). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The two profiles share no compatible capability: capabilities_incompatible (returned with HTTP 200 inside a UCP response). Step 3: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): POST /checkout-sessions with UCP-Agent. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Checkout with ap2.merchant_authorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The signature is missing or does not verify against the merchant's keys: merchant_authorization_missing or merchant_authorization_invalid the platform must not show the checkout. If The merchant needs buyer input it cannot get through the API: status requires_escalation with continue_url the shopper finishes on the merchant's site. Step 5: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Verify the merchant signature, hand off to the trusted UI. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Shopper to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Review and approve choose Google Pay. Step 7: Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface) to Google Pay (credential provider): Run the com.google.pay handler (PAN_ONLY). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The merchant's PSP cannot process Google's tokens: The merchant cannot accept this handler Google's FAQ makes PSP support a precondition. Step 8: Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface) to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Create the closed mandates (per spec live use unverified). Step 9: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): POST /checkout-sessions/ id /complete (signed, with ap2.checkout_mandate). This step crosses a trust boundary. If AP2 was negotiated but ap2.checkout_mandate is missing: mandate_required the merchant must reject the complete. If The response to complete is lost: Retry with the same Idempotency-Key during complete_in_progress the platform must not start a new update or complete. Step 10: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): Verify the checkout mandate against the current checkout. If The mandate is for another checkout, expired or badly signed: mandate_scope_mismatch, mandate_expired or mandate_invalid_signature. Step 11: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor): Authorize the Google Pay token processor checks the payment mandate. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor) to Card network and issuer: Card authorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The issuer declines: The merchant returns a payment failure in the checkout no order is created. Step 13: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): completed with order receipts. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 14: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Order webhook, RFC 9421 signed. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The webhook signer is not the order's business: The platform must reject the event.
